title: Once-for-All: Train One Network and Specialize it for Efficient Deployment
grouping: Three stages left to right, each a dotted rectangle holding a stack of channels with a plain caption under it ('train with full width', 'progressively shrink the width'); between stages a rounded black-outlined column of numbers with arrows labelled 'channel sorting' and 'reorg.'. Later stages nest smaller dotted rectangles inside the outer one.
shapes_depth: Channels are flat coloured parallelograms (grey, orange, green, blue) stacked vertically like sheets, re-ordered from stage to stage. Channel importance is printed as decimals in a tall rounded box. Each nested dotted rectangle has a small arrow out of its lower-right corner labelled O1, O2, O3 for the output of that sub-network.
proposed_highlight: No baseline; the mechanism is shown by the same four coloured channels being re-sorted by importance and enclosed in shrinking nested boxes.
lesson: Show elastic width as the same coloured channel sheets re-sorted between stages by a printed column of importance scores, with nested dotted boxes marking each sub-network's channel subset and its own output tap.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2020'). Figure 1 of this paper was cropped with its top line cut, so figure 6 was carded.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: family other = neural architecture search / once-for-all supernet; architecture other = weight-sharing elastic supernetwork

core.what: three dotted-rectangle stages left to right, each a stack of coloured channel sheets, with channel-importance number columns between them and nested dotted boxes marking ever-smaller sub-networks

relations.form: three dotted rectangles in a row, captioned 'train with full width', then 'progressively shrink the width' twice, joined by arrows labelled 'channel sorting' and 'reorg.'
the sort - reorganise - shrink step is drawn twice in sequence, with a trailing 'channel sorting' arrow out of the last stage implying it continues
nested smaller dotted rectangles inside later stages enclose the top channels of each sub-network, each with its own output arrow O1, O2, O3
four coloured parallelogram sheets stand for channels and keep their colour while their order changes after sorting, so the reordering is seen on the channels themselves
between stages a rounded black-outlined column of importance scores (0.02, 0.15, 0.85, 0.63, then 0.82, 0.11, 0.46) sits on the main horizontal arrow, between 'channel sorting' and 'reorg.'

channels.colour: colour = channel identity (grey, orange, green, blue), held constant across stages so movement is traceable
channels.shape: parallelogram = a channel; rounded box of numbers = importance scores
channels.line: solid black arrows = process steps and outputs O_i
channels.frame: dotted rectangle = one (sub-)network width; nesting = smaller width shares weights with the larger

quality.strengths: Colour has one meaning, channel identity, so the effect of sorting is visible as the same sheets changing order; nested dotted boxes make weight sharing between widths a containment relation, each with its own output O_i; arrows are short and on one horizontal line.
quality.weaknesses: The importance columns have four scores before the second stage but only three in the second, and which score belongs to which sheet is only inferable by order; captions repeat 'progressively shrink the width' verbatim, and the score columns are drawn in the same black rounded box style a module would get.

insights.structure: Three dotted-rectangle stages left to right, each holding a vertical stack of channel sheets with a caption below ('train with full width', 'progressively shrink the width' twice); between stages a rounded black-outlined column of channel-importance numbers with arrows labelled 'channel sorting' and 'reorg.'.
insights.data: Channels are flat coloured parallelograms (grey, orange, green, blue) that keep their colour as they are re-ordered between stages; importance scores are printed decimals; nested smaller dotted rectangles mark each sub-network's channel subset.
insights.emphasis: The same coloured sheets visibly change order after sorting, and each nested dotted box has its own output arrow O1, O2, O3 at its lower right, so the shrinking sub-networks read as nested.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right along straight black arrows, from full width through the importance column to each shrunken stage; the last stage ends with a trailing 'channel sorting' arrow.
insights.avoid: The nested dotted rectangles in the third stage are very close together and their O1/O2/O3 taps overlap, making it hard to tell which box each output belongs to.

arrangement.units: three dotted rectangles, each a stage, with nested smaller dotted rectangles inside later stages; captions below each; connectors are rounded number boxes between stages
arrangement.inputs_as: the full-width channel stack in the first dotted box
arrangement.shared: the same four coloured channel sheets appear in every stage
